Which VIX value is used for date t?.answer: Rule: for every S&P 500 trading date *t*, the VIX feature value is the VIX close from the immediately preceding date in the S&P 500 trading calendar, not the previous row of the VIX dataset. How well do the bankruptcy models perfor.answer:
Company-distress baselines, frozen held-out test (1364 rows, 44 with label 1):
- dummy (`dummy`): average precision 0.032 [0.032, 0.032], ROC-AUC 0.500.
- logistic_regression (`lr_quantile`): average precision 0.472 [0.354, 0.616], ROC-AUC 0.940.
- xgboost (`xgb_large_as_missing`): average precision 0.487 [0.364, 0.637], ROC-AUC 0.958.
- Label 1 is the minority class and is treated as the class to detect. The meanings of labels 0 and 1 are not documented by UCI and remain unverified; no result here should be read as predicting bankruptcy.

The test set does not distinguish Logistic Regression from XGBoost: the interval for their difference includes zero. [1] Probabilities are not calibrated. [2] Applying the models elsewhere could systematically misjudge companies. [3]
